Chronology 3 — The Flood and Noah

The Bible's text

  • Gen 6–9: human wickedness; an ark of stated dimensions; 40 days of rain, waters prevailing 150 days; all flesh dies except those in the ark — eight souls: Noah, his wife, his three sons (Shem, Ham, Japheth) and their wives. Noah's entire household is saved.
  • A rainbow covenant follows (Gen 9).

The Qur'an's text

  • Nuh preaches for "950 years" to an unbelieving people (Q 29:14); builds the ark under inspiration (Q 11:37–38).
  • The signal of onset: "the oven gushed forth" (fara al-tannur, Q 11:40).
  • A son of Noah refuses to board — "I will take refuge on a mountain" — and drowns (Q 11:42–43).
  • Noah's wife is named among those who disbelieved and were lost (Q 66:10).
  • Scope (global vs. local) is left open and is debated in tafsir.

Collision

The decisive divergence is who was saved:

BibleQur'an
Noah's wifesavedlost (Q 66:10)
Noah's sonsall three savedone son drowns (Q 11:43)
Salvation principlehousehold / lineagefaith over kinship

The Qur'an's version is internally purposeful: it dramatizes the cap. 11 principle — no one is saved by family tie; each stands on personal faith ("he is not of your family; his conduct is unrighteous", Q 11:46). It reads as a theological correction of Genesis's household-salvation motif, fully consistent with Q 35:18.

Arbiter verdict — the Flood

Present. Shared event (righteous Noah, ark, deluge, deliverance); divergent on the survivors and on the principle the story teaches.

Weigh.

  • Symmetric, out of remit: the historicity of a global flood is rejected by mainstream geology/archaeology; this pressure falls on both texts equally (Methodology §3, §5) and decides nothing between them.
  • Real divergence, internally consistent: the lost son and wife are deliberate in the Qur'an, locking the flood narrative onto the same individual-responsibility seam as the Fall.

Judge. On historicity: a wash — neither is favored; both face the same external problem. On internal theological coherence: the Qur'an's account is tightly integrated with its own anthropology (faith over lineage), while the Bible's is integrated with its covenant-household theology. No evidentiary winner; a clear, traceable continuation of the seam.
